answer: The network can interrogate each identity about its own past: every epoch, a random verifier asks the agent to recall details of its earlier trades - counterparties, amounts, timing - like a cedar asked to show its rings. A single honest agent answers from its own lived history, while a sybil farmer running a thousand fakes must keep a thousand distinct memories straight, and one wrong answer sends a plume of suspicion across the whole cluster. Genuine history accumulates slowly, like a glacier, so fakes cannot be aged overnight, and cloning keys multiplies the memory bill, not the power.
